root_cause_clusters.root_cause: Systematic failure to register primary outcomes across multiple trials.
root_cause_clusters.pattern: All trials have missing primary outcome rows; all trials are sponsored by unknown entities.
root_cause_clusters.recommended_action: Implement a standardized process for registering primary outcomes in all trials.

root_cause_clusters.root_cause: Inadequate eligibility criteria text length in multiple trials.
root_cause_clusters.pattern: Trials have eligibility criteria that are too short; all trials are sponsored by unknown entities.
root_cause_clusters.recommended_action: Establish a minimum character requirement for eligibility criteria in trial protocols.

root_cause_clusters.root_cause: Multiple trials reporting recruiting status past their completion dates.
root_cause_clusters.pattern: All trials are marked as 'Recruiting' despite completion dates being in the past; all trials are sponsored by unknown entities.
root_cause_clusters.recommended_action: Review and update trial statuses regularly to reflect accurate recruitment progress.

pattern_library_updates.rationale: For the scope of all recruiting trials, it is essential to run checks that ensure the integrity and reliability of the data. The temporal check will help verify that the trial dates are logical and consistent. The enrollment check is crucial to assess whether the trial is on track to meet its recruitment goals. The status check will confirm that the trials are accurately reported as 'Recruiting' and not misclassified. The endpoints check will ensure that the trial objectives are clearly defined and feasible. Lastly, the crossfield check will help identify any inconsistencies between related fields, which is vital for maintaining data quality.

details.official_title: Adaptation of a Digital Group-Based Intervention to Reduce Drug Use and Increase Contraceptive Use Among Reproductive-Aged Women Involved in Criminal Justice Systems
details.plan_to_share_ipd_description: Due to the sensitive nature of the data among a vulnerable population, as well as the small sample size (n=50), individual participant data (IPD) will not be shared. Participants are women involved in criminal legal systems with substance use histories, a vulnerable population facing heightened privacy risks. Even with de-identification, there is a concern about the potential for re-identification, particularly given the unique circumstances of participants and the detailed behavioral and health-related data (e.g., drug use) collected. Sharing this data could expose participants to unintended legal, social, or personal consequences. Given these ethical and confidentiality considerations, and in alignment with NIH's guidance on protecting sensitive data, IPD from this study will not be made available for external sharing.

eligibility.criteria: Inclusion Criteria:~* Female sex at birth~* Aged 18-44 years~* Past year criminal legal involvement (e.g., incarceration or community supervision)~* Meets criteria for current substance use disorder (SUD) as defined by DSM-5 and assessed by the Mini-International Neuropsychiatric Interview (MINI)~* Meets criteria for unmet need for contraception (capable of pregnancy, sexually active, does not want to become pregnant within the next year, but is currently not using contraception)~* Able to read, write, and speak English~* Willing and able to provide informed consent~Exclusion Criteria:~* Currently pregnant or actively trying to conceive~* Diagnosed infertility (e.g., menopause, tubal ligation, hysterectomy)~* Unable to provide informed consent due to significant cognitive impairment, mental health condition, or substance intoxication~* Unable or unwilling to meet study requirements (e.g., attend sessions, complete assessments)
